ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The upper part of the figure gives two spectra. The nonzero range of X₁(ω) is from -B₁ to +B₁, and the middle segment is in the shape of rectangular steps, therefore its highest frequency boundary is B₁. X₂(ω) is a triangular spectrum with ω=0 as the peak value, and the nonzero range is from -B₂ to +B₂, therefore its highest frequency boundary is B₂. The lower system block diagram shows that x₁(t) and x₂(t) first enter a multiplier to be multiplied, and then the result passes through an LTI system with impulse response h(t)=e^{-2|t|}, with the output being y(t). Reasoning: The signal after the multiplier input is z(t)=x₁(t)x₂(t). Time-domain multiplication corresponds to frequency-domain convolution, so Z(ω)=(1/2π)[X₁(ω)*X₂(ω)]. Since X₁(ω) is supported on [-B₁,B₁], and X₂(ω) is supported on [-B₂,B₂], the support range after convolution is [-(B₁+B₂), +(B₁+B₂)]. Subsequently y(t)=z(t)*h(t), therefore Y(ω)=Z(ω)H(ω). The frequency response of h(t)=e^{-2|t|} only changes the amplitude shape and will not expand the nonzero frequency support of Z(ω), so the bandwidth of y(t) is B₁+B₂. According to the Nyquist sampling theorem, the minimum sampling rate is twice the highest frequency, namely 2(B₁+B₂).

method.method_draft: Identify the input to the filter as z(t)=x1(t)x2(t). From the plotted spectra, X1 has bandwidth B1 and X2 has bandwidth B2. Compute Z(ω)=(1/2π)(X1*X2)(ω), whose nonzero interval is from -(B1+B2) to +(B1+B2). Since y(t)=z(t)*h(t), Y(ω)=Z(ω)H(ω); the exponential impulse response changes amplitudes but not the maximum occupied frequency. Therefore y(t) is bandlimited to B1+B2, so the minimum sampling rate is 2(B1+B2).

图像描述：图中上方给出了两个频谱。X₁(ω) 的非零范围从 -B₁ 到 +B₁，中间分段为矩形台阶形状，因此其最高频率边界是 B₁。X₂(ω) 是以 ω=0 为峰值的三角形频谱，非零范围从 -B₂ 到 +B₂，因此其最高频率边界是 B₂。下方系统框图显示 x₁(t) 和 x₂(t) 先进入乘法器相乘，然后结果通过冲激响应 h(t)=e^{-2|t|} 的 LTI 系统，输出为 y(t)。

In the figure, \( h(t) = e^{-2|t|} \) denotes the impulse response. For the system shown in the figure, what is the minimum sampling rate required to sample \( y(t) \) so that \( y(t) \) can be uniquely reconstructed from its samples?
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: The upper part of the figure gives two spectra. The nonzero range of X₁(ω) is from -B₁ to +B₁, and the middle segment is in the shape of rectangular steps, therefore its highest frequency boundary is B₁. X₂(ω) is a triangular spectrum with ω=0 as the peak value, and the nonzero range is from -B₂ to +B₂, therefore its highest frequency boundary is B₂. The lower system block diagram shows that x₁(t) and x₂(t) first enter a multiplier to be multiplied, and then the result passes through an LTI system with impulse response h(t)=e^{-2|t|}, with the output being y(t).

Reasoning: The signal after the multiplier input is z(t)=x₁(t)x₂(t). Time-domain multiplication corresponds to frequency-domain convolution, so Z(ω)=(1/2π)[X₁(ω)*X₂(ω)]. Since X₁(ω) is supported on [-B₁,B₁], and X₂(ω) is supported on [-B₂,B₂], the support range after convolution is [-(B₁+B₂), +(B₁+B₂)]. Subsequently y(t)=z(t)*h(t), therefore Y(ω)=Z(ω)H(ω). The frequency response of h(t)=e^{-2|t|} only changes the amplitude shape and will not expand the nonzero frequency support of Z(ω), so the bandwidth of y(t) is B₁+B₂. According to the Nyquist sampling theorem, the minimum sampling rate is twice the highest frequency, namely 2(B₁+B₂).
